prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from persistent storage during OAuthClientProvider._initialize() never get token_expiry_time recomputed, so is_token_valid() treats an already-expired stored access token as valid, the proactive pre-request refresh check is skipped, and the client falls through to a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from persistent storage during OAuthClientProvider._initialize() never get token_expiry_time recomputed, so is_token_valid() treats an already-expired stored access token as valid, the proactive pre-request refresh check is skipped, and the client falls through to a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 fixes the root cause directly: it calls context.update_token_expiry(current_tokens) right inside _initialize() as soon as stored tokens are loaded, so every downstream check (is_token_valid, the proactive-refresh branch, 401 handling) sees correct expiry data, and it adds a dedicated expired_tokens fixture/test covering the load-from-storage case. #2875 does not touch _initialize(); its own inline comment states the added 401-path 'try stored refresh_token before full re-auth' step exists only because 'a provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time' — i.e. it patches the symptom in the reactive 401 branch rather than the data that's wrong, and its extra branch becomes dead weight once the expiry value is fixed at the source.

prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs address unhandled failure when the StreamableHTTP SSE reconnection logic ultimately gives up: the client currently leaves the caller with no usable signal that the stream/request has permanently failed. #2395 patches `_handle_reconnection` directly at the exhausted-retry branch, sending a proper JSONRPCError through `read_stream_writer` so the specific in-flight request that was awaiting a resumed response gets an error instead of hanging forever (with an isinstance guard so it only applies to JSONRPCRequest messages, not notifications). #3098 instead adds a generic `_unwrap_exception` helper that walks anyio ExceptionGroup trees to recover a `StreamableHTTPError` and re-raise it as a clean, catchable type, addressing the case where the underlying failure is currently buried inside an opaque ExceptionGroup at the task-group/context-manager level. prs.title: fix(server): don't raise when tool_use is not followed by tool_result
prs.author: Bartok9
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs touch the exact same lines in validate_tool_use_result_messages to address the same reported bug (#2960): when an assistant tool_use is not followed by any tool_result, the function incorrectly raises 'ids of tool_result blocks and tool_use blocks from previous message do not match' (a misleading mismatch error, since tool_result_ids is simply empty). The two PRs resolve it with opposite semantics: #2962 adds a has_tool_results guard so the ID-mismatch check is skipped entirely when there are no tool_results, meaning no error is raised at all in this case — its test cites SEP-1577, which requires tool_result to be preceded by tool_use but does NOT require tool_use to be followed by a tool_result. #3053 instead keeps this as an error case but replaces the confusing message with an explicit 'tool_use blocks must be followed by matching tool_result blocks', which asserts the opposite validation requirement. (2 PRs)

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a process restart, OAuthClientProvider._refresh_token() needs the authorization server's OAuthMetadata (token endpoint, issuer) to build the refresh request, but that metadata was only ever kept in memory during the original interactive OAuth flow, so a reloaded provider has no metadata and token refresh after restart breaks or has to fall back to full re-authorization. prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3263 fixes cold-start refresh for any TokenStorage implementation by re-running AS metadata discovery on demand before the refresh call, and additionally adds an issuer-binding check on the discovered metadata, closing a mixup-attack gap; it requires no changes to the TokenStorage interface. #2492 instead adds new optional get_oauth_metadata/set_oauth_metadata methods to the TokenStorage protocol that default to no-op, so the fix is inert unless a given storage backend is separately updated to implement them, leaving existing/third-party TokenStorage implementations still broken after restart until they opt in.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 fixes the failure at its source in `_handle_reconnection` (the exhausted-retries branch) and restores the normal request/response contract by sending a proper JSONRPCError through the existing read_stream_writer path that callers already await on, with an isinstance(...,JSONRPCRequest) guard to avoid misapplying it to notifications. #3098's `_unwrap_exception` helper only recovers a StreamableHTTPError after it's already been wrapped in an ExceptionGroup, which only helps callers observing the outer task group/context-manager exit and does not resolve the underlying issue of an individual in-flight request hanging indefinitely -- a narrower, later-stage patch over the same root cause.

members.title: fix(server): don't raise when tool_use is not followed by tool_result
members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs touch the exact same lines in validate_tool_use_result_messages to address the same reported bug (#2960): when an assistant tool_use is not followed by any tool_result, the function incorrectly raises 'ids of tool_result blocks and tool_use blocks from previous message do not match' (a misleading mismatch error, since tool_result_ids is simply empty). The two PRs resolve it with opposite semantics: #2962 adds a has_tool_results guard so the ID-mismatch check is skipped entirely when there are no tool_results, meaning no error is raised at all in this case — its test cites SEP-1577, which requires tool_result to be preceded by tool_use but does NOT require tool_use to be followed by a tool_result. #3053 instead keeps this as an error case but replaces the confusing message with an explicit 'tool_use blocks must be followed by matching tool_result blocks', which asserts the opposite validation requirement. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 fixes the failure at its source in `_handle_reconnection` (the exhausted-retries branch) and restores the normal request/response contract by sending a proper JSONRPCError through the existing read_stream_writer path that callers already await on, with an isinstance(...,JSONRPCRequest) guard to avoid misapplying it to notifications. #3098's `_unwrap_exception` helper only recovers a StreamableHTTPError after it's already been wrapped in an ExceptionGroup, which only helps callers observing the outer task group/context-manager exit and does not resolve the underlying issue of an individual in-flight request hanging indefinitely -- a narrower, later-stage patch over the same root cause.

members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs address unhandled failure when the StreamableHTTP SSE reconnection logic ultimately gives up: the client currently leaves the caller with no usable signal that the stream/request has permanently failed. #2395 patches `_handle_reconnection` directly at the exhausted-retry branch, sending a proper JSONRPCError through `read_stream_writer` so the specific in-flight request that was awaiting a resumed response gets an error instead of hanging forever (with an isinstance guard so it only applies to JSONRPCRequest messages, not notifications). #3098 instead adds a generic `_unwrap_exception` helper that walks anyio ExceptionGroup trees to recover a `StreamableHTTPError` and re-raise it as a clean, catchable type, addressing the case where the underlying failure is currently buried inside an opaque ExceptionGroup at the task-group/context-manager level. clusters.pick_reason: #2962's fix is backed by an explicit spec citation (SEP-1577) showing that a tool_use not followed by a tool_result is valid and should not raise at all, whereas #3053's fix continues to reject that same valid case with a differently-worded error, contradicting the cited spec. #2962's regression test documents this spec rationale directly in the test docstring, giving reviewers a verifiable justification that #3053's test lacks.

members.title: fix(server): don't raise when tool_use is not followed by tool_result
members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs touch the exact same lines in validate_tool_use_result_messages to address the same reported bug (#2960): when an assistant tool_use is not followed by any tool_result, the function incorrectly raises 'ids of tool_result blocks and tool_use blocks from previous message do not match' (a misleading mismatch error, since tool_result_ids is simply empty). The two PRs resolve it with opposite semantics: #2962 adds a has_tool_results guard so the ID-mismatch check is skipped entirely when there are no tool_results, meaning no error is raised at all in this case — its test cites SEP-1577, which requires tool_result to be preceded by tool_use but does NOT require tool_use to be followed by a tool_result. #3053 instead keeps this as an error case but replaces the confusing message with an explicit 'tool_use blocks must be followed by matching tool_result blocks', which asserts the opposite validation requirement. (2 PRs)
